newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures slipped into the red late on Wednesday amid weakness in other bond markets on concerns about the need for further interest rate rises in the United States, traders said.

They said the mood remained cautious ahead of a key U.S. jobs report due on Friday and government bond sales on Thursday and if the US data were to come in stronger than expected 10-year yields of six percent could be targetted.
Some analysts, however, said they thought the selloff in France was already running out of steam and that there was little to fear from European economic fundamentals.

"We're bouncing around in the (127).40 to 60 range and it should be difficult to see much of a breakout on the downside," Joanne Perez, bond strategist at Merrill Lynch in Paris said. "I still don't think fundamentally there's much to fear and we're close to stabilization on the (US) long-bond."
Some traders, however, said they expected the June contract to test support at 127.00 sometime before the US jobs data.

The June contract fell as low as 127.26 on Wednesday, an area of support near March 20 lows, but recovered to settle at 127.40. The contract ticked slightly higher on GLOBEX after a US factory orders report came in marginally weaker than feared.
Some traders said the late selloff, while sparked by declines in Germany and the United States, had been exacerbated by domestic banks selling futures to cover franc bond issues earlier in the day.

There was little concern about the sale of 20 to 22 billion francs of OATs on Thursday. Analysts said the slightly smaller auction size than in recent months coupled with some 47 billion francs due in coupon payments in April would ease the pain.
The fact the sale was spread across the 10-year benchmark, the cheapest to deliver OAT and a variable rate OAT was also helping ease concerns about the auction, analysts said.
"The TEC (variable rate OAT) has held up over the last few weeks because the curve has steepened so much. We've good demand for the 2009 and the 2006," Perez said.
The 10-year spread between OATs and Bunds held steady at minus 10 basis points on Wednesday.
Still some traders said investors were reluctant to buy paper at the moment and there could well be some covering ahead of Thursday's sale. The results will be released from 0900 GMT.
There was also some concern among traders that 10-year Bund yields, which have been hovering around six percent this week, could eventually jump higher, dragging French yields up as well.
The curve steepened again on Wednesday, the gap between two and 10-year yields rising four basis points.

Traders said French interest rate futures received an early boost from non-resident buying, mainly from a British house, but struggled to break through resistance at 96.65. The contract slipped back to 96.62 at the close.
The franc remained stable below 3.37 per mark.
